summary:
What if the Earth could tell us its story, not through charts, numbers or satellite images, but through music?

Every rise in temperature, shift in wind, change in vegetation and pulse of wildfire tells us something about our planet. TerraSonus - The Earth Information Jukebox, built by Team ASGARD, lets you hear that story.

TerraSonus is an interactive web application that transforms climate and environmental data into structured musical patterns. Through a 3D globe, six guided exploration tracks and an interactive Climate Time Machine covering 1980-2026, users can explore how Earth's conditions have changed over time through both sight and sound.

At its core, TerraSonus features a sound engine that maps environmental variables to distinct audio patterns. Its Visual Sonifier takes this further by transforming image pixel information into sound, creating another way to experience visual environmental data.

Accessibility is built into the experience through speech narration, keyboard controls and a dedicated Blind Access mode, allowing more people to explore and interact with environmental information.

Inspired by NASA's Earth-observation work and the possibilities of open environmental data, TerraSonus explores a new way to make complex planetary changes more engaging, accessible and understandable.

Earth's story deserves to be experienced, not just observed. Sometimes, the most powerful way to understand a changing world is to listen.
details:
TerraSonus – The Earth Information Jukebox is an interactive web app that turns climate-related data into structured music. A 3D Earth globe, five regional hotspots, six guided exploration tracks and a Time Machine covering 1980–2026 let users explore how our planet is changing through both sight and sound.

The sonification engine maps environmental variables such as temperature, CO₂, wind, vegetation (NDVI) and wildfire activity to distinct audio patterns, using musical mapping techniques and a pentatonic scale. The Visual Sonifier goes a step further by converting image pixel information into sound, so users can experience visual data by listening to it.

TerraSonus supports inclusive exploration with speech narration, keyboard controls, ARIA support, Blind Access mode and an in-app Sound Guide. We want to make Earth science more accessible, interactive and engaging, especially for people who run into barriers with visual information.

The project was inspired by NASA’s Earth-observation work and open environmental data, and it explores new ways of presenting planetary information. The current app uses embedded climate reference values, and we plan to integrate live NASA data in future development.

We built it with React, Vite, JavaScript, Three.js, Tone.js, the Web Audio API, Tailwind CSS and the Web Speech API, and deployed it on Cloudflare Pages.

The creativity of TerraSonus lies in turning environmental information into a musical experience. By bringing together data, sound, visualization and accessibility, we hope to offer a new way to understand and connect with our changing planet. While building it, we kept accessibility, musical clarity, meaningful data representation, user experience, technical feasibility and future scalability in mind
